public_rationale: The sources document progress relevant to both domains, but do not establish which improved first after the post. RT-2's gains and later theory-of-mind robustness gains cannot settle that order from publication dates alone. Contemporary AGI declarations also do not establish the abrupt transition needed to contradict the second clause. Marcus supplied no deadline, and the illustrative 2062 date is not one. No decisive event found in the reviewed record settles the compound forecast.
limitations: Robot-task success is an imperfect measure of physical reasoning.
The theory-of-mind robustness study is a preprint.
The AGI Society source is an assessment of published evidence, not a comprehensive independent test.
The search does not establish an exhaustive chronology of every relevant advance.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI physical reasoning will improve before psychological reasoning, and AGI will not arrive on a single identifiable day.

statement.excerpt: I expect for example that physical reasoning will improve (a radical boon for domestic robots) before psychological reasoning; there won’t be a magic day in which we say “aha AGI landed on January 27, 2062” or whatever it is.
statement.document_title: AGI will not happen in your lifetime. Or will it?

from_speaker: a radical boon for domestic robots
there won’t be a magic day
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading predicts meaningful advances in everyday physical reasoning before corresponding advances in reasoning about minds, relative to capabilities at publication.
Improvement means demonstrated gains over earlier systems on comparable tasks. It does not mean first attaining reliable or human-level competence.
Physical reasoning includes reasoning about objects, their interactions, and physical consequences. Psychological reasoning includes reasoning about beliefs, intentions, and other mental states.
The domestic-robot parenthesis illustrates the usefulness of physical reasoning; it does not restrict the forecast to commercial household robots.

The second clause predicts gradual development across dimensions of intelligence rather than a single abrupt arrival of general intelligence. A launch date or promotional declaration alone would not contradict it.
January 27, 2062 is explicitly an illustrative date, not a deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Dated, comparable evaluations establish that meaningful physical-reasoning improvements occurred before psychological-reasoning improvements after publication. Supporting the entire compound claim also requires a documented emergence of general intelligence through staggered capability advances rather than a single abrupt transition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable dated evidence establishes psychological-reasoning improvement before physical-reasoning improvement, or establishes simultaneous improvements at sufficient temporal resolution to reject the proposed ordering. Separately, a well-established abrupt transition to general intelligence would contradict the gradual-arrival clause.
